newsitem.title: USA: Cotton production, consumption in balance - ICAC.
newsitem.headline: Cotton production, consumption in balance - ICAC.

text.p: World cotton production and consumption are expected to be closely balanced this season and next, offering price stability in the two-year period, the International Cotton Advisory Committee said Monday.
No large changes in world ending stocks are foreseen for either season, the group said in its monthly outlook.
The Cotlook A Index is expected to average 76 cents per pound in 1996/97 and 78 cents per pound in 1997/98. It averaged 86 cents last season.
The group estimated world production at 19.01 million tonnes (87.3 million bales) in 1996/97, down from 19.96 million tonnes (91.7 million bales) in 1995/96.

It put consumption at 19.25 million tonnes (88.4 million bales) in 1996/97, up from 18.626 million tonnes (85.5 million bales) the previous year. The group projected 1997/98 production at 19.73 million tonnes (90.6 million bales) and consumption at 19.62 million tonnes (90.1 million bales).
World exports would fall to 5.78 million tonnes (26.6 million bales) in 1996/97 from 6.212 million tonnes (28.5 million bales) in 1995/96.
The 40 governments who make up the committee will meet Oct 6-11 in Tashkent, Uzbekistan in plenary session, ICAC said.
